title: ORBIT-Q Task Atlas
lede: What each benchmark task actually tests, which representation makes it tractable, and where agent-framework workflows fail.

blocks.label: Agent-framework co-performance
blocks.why: ORBIT-Q evaluates agent-framework co-performance on complete scientific workflows: numerical correctness is combined with semantic framework fidelity and submitted-artifact runtime.

pairs: 1.13×–21.81× the expert reference across 26 valid published timing pairs [Survey inference]

blocks.label: Interpretation boundary
blocks.text: Framework results measure agent-mediated framework usability and performance, not the best possible expert-written implementation for every framework.

blocks.label: Competing-interest context
blocks.text: The ORBIT-Q authors disclose that they are also the authors of TensorCircuit-NG, the framework used for the expert reference implementations.

rows: 01 · DMRG-MPS Input With Variational Circuit Refinement
External MPS input + differentiable circuit tensor network
A finite 500-step energy history whose refined energy remains consistent with the supplied DMRG reference.
Statevector or tensor network with half-chain reduced density matrices
Energy and total loss both decrease, with a correctly recomputed final entropy-profile MSE.
Unnormalized branch state + differentiable event probabilities
Energy and loss decrease while success probability remains consistent with the 60-event mean log probability.
04 · Trainable Kraus Noise Calibration From Multi-Circuit Data
Both transition probabilities are recovered within 2e-4 and the fitted channel is trace preserving.
The energy density decreases to within 0.5 of the exact sparse ground-state density without crossing below it.
06 · Digital-Analog Hybrid VQE With Trainable Analog Blocks
Energy improves while all learned analog parameters remain in their specified open bounds.
Trajectory batch with classical branch-dependent feedback
The average energy improves by at least 0.3, reaches at most -8.3, and returns 64 final trajectory energies.
Returned samples meet shape/binary checks and hidden Z-string error tolerances.
Backward causal cones of 15 and 18 qubits
Mean objective improves and the best final local objective reaches at least 1.0.
Matrix-free state update or structured diagonal tensor
Energy improves and finishes within 0.25 density units of the sparse exact reference.
11 · Spin-1 Haldane-Chain VQE With String-Order Verification
Energy is close to exact and the three string correlators have mean absolute error at most 0.12.
12 · Variational Circuit to MPS Overlap Optimization
Fidelity improves to at least 0.85 with valid loss, parameter, and overlap-phase outputs.

blocks.label: Reading the pattern
blocks.text: Symbols follow TensorCircuit-NG, PennyLane, TorchQuantum, and MindQuantum. ✓ and × redundantly encode pass/fail without relying on color.

blocks.label: Survey taxonomy
blocks.why: ORBIT-Q defines 12 workflows; these five clusters are an analytical organization, not an official taxonomy.

rows: External MPS states must connect directly to differentiable circuit computations.
Optimization is constrained by entanglement, continuous-time dynamics, or measurement-conditioned control flow.
Differentiation must survive post-selection, Kraus maps, or repeated non-unitary normalization.
The requested representation—not a dense fallback—is the central computational test.
A low energy alone is insufficient; qutrit semantics and nonlocal string order must also agree.

items.caption: Published framework-axis validity for the fixed Codex agent. Blue ✓ cells passed the full validity pipeline; orange × cells did not. This is agent-mediated evidence, not a proof of absolute framework impossibility.

rows: Timeouts, missing artifacts, exceptions, or numerical evaluator failures.
A custom simulator or contraction replaces the required framework-native computation.
A cheaper objective, reduced ansatz, or omitted physical component passes some surface checks.
The agent cannot find or compose a native representation, gate, or control-flow feature.
Contraction, differentiation, memory, or trajectory costs make the chosen representation impractical.
A refusal, tool policy, or agent workflow prevents a valid artifact.

blocks.label: Qualification
blocks.text: Framework results measure agent-mediated framework usability and performance, not the best possible expert-written implementation for every framework.

blocks.label: Policy distinction
blocks.text: A method can solve the physics without satisfying ORBIT-Q's framework-native policy. External solvers are alternatives or references, not automatically valid submissions.

blocks.title: Prioritized roadmap · Survey inference
items: 1. Add rolling or private tasks and stronger runtime provenance.
2. Use blinded or multi-auditor semantic review.
3. Build expert baselines for frameworks beyond TensorCircuit-NG.
4. Broaden task families, including QEC simulation and decoding.
5. Record gradient and memory-complexity diagnostics for scalability claims.
